name: Compare a fixed count with two performances of the same score

uses.action: Align three wheel spokes and a rest, then play the figure through a suspended rim and a floorboard. Fen can agree on a one-beat value while the shell gives the silence a different emotional meaning.

name: Adjust craft pressure using the material’s response

uses.action: Run the notched stylus over the same tabs under light, working and heavy pressure. Ease up when the hollow fills in, and hand Fen a grip that distinguishes two profiles on worn wood.

name: Stage two translations of a verse and hear what changes

uses.action: Lay a literal line and a three-pulse line against the same fall of a fruit. The first leaves the fruit unnamed and arrives late. The second lands the prop on the beat and specifies a plum.
Take both renderings to the actor in the forest. Change fruit or timing and let the child in the audience supply a new word. Rehearse again to reverse the choice.

name: Distinguish the count of a rest from what a performer values in it

uses.action: Fit the gap to the last empty beat on Fen’s wheel. Hear what waiting for a child to answer does to the same silence. Fen keeps a common entrance and each player’s reason for the wait.
